If business assets of a business (permanent establishment) located in Austria are transferred abroad to another business (permanent establishment), the business assets transferred abroad shall be measured at the values that would have been applied in the case of a supply or other service to a business entirely independent of the taxpayer, if

— the foreign business belongs to the same taxpayer,
— the taxpayer is a co-entrepreneur of the foreign business,
— the taxpayer holds a substantial interest, i.e. more than 25%, in the foreign corporation, or
— the same persons exercise management or control over both businesses or have influence on them.

Participations and loan receivables in companies with registered office or place of management abroad may, under the following conditions, be recognized in the year of acquisition at a value of 90% of the acquisition costs:
a) The funds are used for a permanent establishment abroad which serves the distribution, setting up or servicing of goods produced in Austria.
b) In the case of corporations, there must be
— significant participations (participation of more than 25% in the share capital) acquired upon formation or a capital increase, or
— shareholder loans from substantial shareholders, if the loans were granted upon formation or a considerable expansion of the company.
c) In the case of partnerships in which the partners are considered co-entrepreneurs, significant participations within the meaning of letter (b) acquired upon formation or a considerable expansion of the company must exist.

1. a) emoluments and benefits from an existing or former employment relationship.

c) emoluments from a statutory sickness or accident insurance. 
d) emoluments from a foreign statutory sickness or accident insurance which corresponds to a domestic sickness or accident insurance. 
e) sickness benefits from the welfare and support institutions of the chambers of self-employed persons.

For buildings serving residential purposes, the following applies with respect to repair and maintenance expenses: 
— Repair and maintenance expenses that are incurred using correspondingly earmarked tax-free subsidies from public funds are, to that extent, excluded from the determination of income. 
— If, after offsetting the losses determined without taking into account the repair and maintenance expenses within the meaning of Section 5(3), there remain tax-free amounts under Section 5, then the repair and maintenance expenses not covered by tax-free subsidies shall be offset against these tax-free amounts. 
— Those repair and maintenance expenses that were not covered by tax-free subsidies and were not required to be offset against tax-free amounts shall be deducted in equal instalments spread over ten years.

— payments for the waiver of work performance for future wage payment periods,
— payments for pension commutations, to the extent that they are not to be taxed pursuant to subsection (6) at the tax rates of subsection (1),
— back payments and subsequent payments of current and other emoluments for expired calendar years, which are made alongside current wages from the same employer or in bankruptcy proceedings and are not based on an arbitrary deferral of the payment date,
— settlement sums, regardless of whether they are based on judicial or extrajudicial settlements, and also in cases where they are not granted alongside current wages from the same employer.
